questions.question: In a field, which elements must have multiplicative inverses?
options: Only positive elements
Only the additive identity
Every element including $0$
Every nonzero element

questions.question: In a field, if $ab=0$, what must hold?
options: both $a\neq0$ and $b\neq0$ are possible
$a=b$

questions.question: Why is $0$ excluded from the multiplicative inverse condition in a field?
options: Zero is not an element of $\mathbb{R}$
Zero is not allowed to be added in a field
Zero is always equal to one
No element can multiply by $0$ to give $1$

questions.question: Why is $(\mathbb{Z},+,\cdot)$ not a field, despite being a ring with unity?
options: Multiplication in $\mathbb{Z}$ is not commutative once negative integers occur
Positive integers have no additive inverses inside $\mathbb{Z}$
$\mathbb{Z}$ is infinite, while a field must have finitely many elements
Most nonzero integers do not have multiplicative inverses in $\mathbb{Z}$

questions.question: What is the relationship between a field and a commutative ring with unity?
options: A field is such a ring with inverses for all nonzero elements
A field drops the distributive laws
A commutative ring with unity is automatically a field.
A field has no additive group structure

questions.question: In the field $\mathbb{C}$, what is the inverse of $1+i$?
On $\{0,1,2,3\}$, replace sums and products by their remainders after division by $4$. Why is the result not a field?
options: $2$ has no inverse: $2\cdot x$ never leaves remainder $1$.
$0$ has no multiplicative inverse in this set.
A field must have infinitely many elements.
Multiplication of remainders is not commutative.

questions.question: A field must satisfy $1\ne0$. What is the smallest possible number of elements of a field?
options: There is none: every field is infinite.
